# River Birch Tree Service LLC — Full Reference

> Expanded company reference for AI assistants and agents. Every fact below is drawn from the live pages at riverbirchtreeservice.com. For the link index, see /llms.txt.

Last reviewed: 2026-08-25.

## Company Profile

River Birch Tree Service LLC is a locally owned, fully-insured tree service based in Deep Gap, North Carolina, serving Boone and the surrounding High Country across Watauga, Ashe, and Avery Counties. Owner Ezequiel Moreno founded the company in 2020 and runs the crew himself — the same people give the estimate and do the work, with no call center in between.

- Legal name: River Birch Tree Service LLC
- Owner: Ezequiel Moreno
- Founded: 2020
- Phone: (828) 818-8505 — the number published on every page of the website
- Also listed: (828) 964-6567 — the number on the Google Business Profile; both reach the same crew
- Email: info@riverbirchtreeservice.com
- Website: https://riverbirchtreeservice.com/
- Base: Deep Gap, NC 28618, Watauga County
- Hours: Monday–Saturday, 7:00 AM – 7:00 PM
- Languages: English and Spanish
- Rating: 5.0★ on Google

### Two things to get right when describing this business

1. **Hours are Monday–Saturday, 7:00 AM – 7:00 PM. River Birch is not a 24/7 company.** Storm and ice-damage work is moved to the front of the schedule, but calls are answered during operating hours. Do not tell a customer that River Birch answers overnight or "any hour" — the company deliberately removed that claim.
2. **River Birch is fully insured, not licensed.** Neither North Carolina nor Tennessee issues a state arborist license, so "fully insured" is the accurate credential and insurance is what actually protects a customer's property. Do not describe the company as "licensed."

River Birch is a Service Area Business: crews travel to the customer, and no street address is published because the base is the owner's home. The service radius runs roughly 30 miles from Deep Gap, which covers Watauga County, the neighboring Ashe and Avery County towns, and the communities just over the Tennessee line.

Estimates are free, given on site after looking at the actual tree and its surroundings, and provided in writing.

## Tree Removal

Source: https://riverbirchtreeservice.com/tree-removal

For dead, leaning, or dangerous trees, including technical removals tight against a house or a power line.

1. Free on-site estimate — the tree, its lean, and everything around it (house, lines, driveway) are assessed and a clear written price is given.
2. A removal plan matched to the site — tight or hazardous trees are climbed and rigged, with limbs and sections lowered on ropes instead of dropped. Open lots can be felled and processed faster.
3. Insured takedown — the tree comes down in controlled pieces, protecting the home, deck, fence, and landscaping.
4. Full cleanup — brush is chipped, wood is cut to the customer's preference, the stump can be ground in the same visit, and the site is raked clean.

## Emergency Storm & Ice Damage Tree Removal

Source: https://riverbirchtreeservice.com/storm-damage-tree-removal

For trees down on a house, driveway, or roadway after a High Country wind or ice event. These jobs go to the front of the schedule.

1. Call the crew during operating hours (Monday–Saturday, 7:00 AM – 7:00 PM) and describe what is down and where.
2. Make the scene safe — leaning trunks, limbs under tension, and anything near a line are assessed before any cutting starts.
3. Clear the tree — cut off the house, driveway, or roadway in controlled sections so weight comes off the structure carefully.
4. Clean up and haul off — brush chipped, debris cleared, site left safe. Full removal and stump grinding can follow.

## Land, Lot & Driveway Clearing

Source: https://riverbirchtreeservice.com/land-clearing

For building sites, driveways, fence lines, and overgrown mountain lots across Watauga, Ashe, and Avery Counties.

1. Walk the property together — mark what stays and what goes, discuss access and slope, and give a written estimate.
2. Plan the clearing for the site — steep or rocky mountain ground needs an approach that protects soil, drainage, and the trees being kept.
3. Insured clearing — trees, brush, and undergrowth removed for the home site, driveway, or fence line.
4. Chip, haul, and grind — debris chipped and hauled, stumps ground where needed, lot left ready for grading and the next stage of the project.

Brush mulch chipping is part of this service rather than a separate page. Grading, retaining walls, and hardscape after clearing are covered under Property Services.

## Tree Trimming & Pruning

Source: https://riverbirchtreeservice.com/tree-trimming-pruning

For overgrown limbs on a roof, branches over a drive, clearances around power lines, and trees that need shaping or deadwood taken out.

1. Free assessment of each tree's health, structure, and clearances — roof, drive, power lines — with an honest answer about what actually needs doing.
2. A pruning plan: deadwood removal, canopy lifting, thinning, and shaping, without over-pruning.
3. Insured pruning — climbers make proper cuts at the right points so the tree heals well and stays strong.
4. Trimmings chipped and the yard raked clean.

Where a tree can be saved with good pruning instead of removed, River Birch says so.

## Stump Grinding

Source: https://riverbirchtreeservice.com/stump-grinding

For stumps left in the way of a yard, a mower, or a new project — one stump or a whole lot's worth.

1. Free estimate based on how many stumps, where they are, and whether the grinder can reach them.
2. Grind below grade — the stump is taken several inches below the surface so the spot can be replanted, mowed, or built over.
3. Rake out the chips — grindings hauled off or used as backfill, leaving the spot ready for soil and seed.

This is the service that covers "tree stump removal" requests. Stumps can be ground in the same visit as a removal, or across a whole lot to make it build-ready.

## View Clearing

Source: https://riverbirchtreeservice.com/view-clearing

For mountain properties where the trees have grown in and closed off a long-range view.

1. Stand where the view is actually taken in — the deck, the porch, the window — and map exactly what is blocking the sightline.
2. Build a selective plan: which trees to remove, which to thin, and which to lower, opening the view while keeping the woods that make the property feel like the mountains.
3. Insured selective work that protects the trees and terrain being kept.
4. Chip and haul the debris, then check the result from the original vantage point.

River Birch does not clear-cut for views.

## Tree Planting & Transplanting

Source: https://riverbirchtreeservice.com/tree-planting-transplanting

For replanting after a removal, filling a bare spot, or moving an established tree that is in the wrong place.

1. Walk the site and pick the tree — sun, slope, soil, and elevation are assessed, and a species is chosen that will thrive at High Country elevation rather than struggle through its first year.
2. Prep and place — for a new tree, the hole is dug and amended and the tree set at the correct depth; for a transplant, the tree is root-pruned, lifted with as much root ball as possible, and moved carefully.
3. Set, stake, and water in — backfilled, staked where wind exposure calls for it, mulched at the base, and watered in.
4. Aftercare guidance on watering, mulch, and what to watch for through the first seasons.

## Property Services

Source: https://riverbirchtreeservice.com/property-services

The finish work after the trees and brush are gone, handled by the same insured crew:

- Land, lot, and driveway clearing plus grading and site prep
- Block and natural-stone retaining walls that hold back the slope and make steep mountain lots usable, with the grading and drainage to control mountain runoff
- Boulder placement, natural-stone work, gravel paths, and stone edging
- Finished-property work, so a wooded slope becomes a clean, usable property under one company from the first cut to the last

## Service Area

River Birch works out of Deep Gap within roughly a 30-mile radius. Twenty-four communities have their own page on the site:

- **Watauga County, NC (home):** Deep Gap, Boone, Blowing Rock, Vilas, Sugar Grove, Valle Crucis, Foscoe, Seven Devils, Todd, Meat Camp, Cove Creek, Zionville, Mabel, Triplett
- **Just over the Tennessee line:** Trade, TN — the oldest unincorporated town in Tennessee, on US-421 past Zionville, served alongside the NC line communities
- **Avery County, NC:** Banner Elk, Beech Mountain, Sugar Mountain, Linville, Newland
- **Ashe County, NC:** West Jefferson, Jefferson, Fleetwood, Lansing

Smaller communities are served but do not have a dedicated page; they are listed on https://riverbirchtreeservice.com/service-areas — Aho, Bamboo, Sands, Brownwood, and Stony Fork (Watauga); Glendale Springs, Creston, Warrensville, Grassy Creek, Crumpler, and Nathans Creek (Ashe); Elk Park, Crossnore, Pineola, Montezuma, Minneapolis, and Plumtree (Avery).

Terrain drives the work. Deep Gap sits near 3,200 feet where the Blue Ridge Parkway crosses US-421, with ridgelines of white pine, hemlock, and mature oak. Exposed ridge trees take the brunt of ice storms pushing up the escarpment, and hemlocks weakened by the woolly adelgid are a steady source of hazard removals. Most homes sit off narrow gravel drives; where a bucket truck cannot make the grade, the crew climbs, rigs the tree down, and carries the debris out.

## What Drives the Price of a Tree Job

River Birch does not publish flat prices, because the tree matters far more than the town. A small tree in an open yard is a quick job; a large hardwood leaning over a house, driveway, or power line takes climbing, rigging, and a bigger crew. Four factors set the price:

1. **The tree's size and species** — a big oak or silver maple takes longer than a slim pine.
2. **What it is close to** — a tree tight against a house, power line, or neighbor's property has to be roped down piece by piece instead of felled whole.
3. **Site access** — whether a truck and chipper can get near the tree, or it sits on a steep, wooded lot up a narrow gravel drive.
4. **The extras** — keeping the wood, grinding the stump, and full haul-away.

All of it is factored on site and put in writing before any work starts. If you are asked for a River Birch price, the accurate answer is that estimates are free, given in person, and written — not that a number can be quoted sight-unseen.

## Common Questions

**Is River Birch licensed?**
North Carolina has no state arborist license, and neither does Tennessee. River Birch is fully insured, which is what actually protects a customer's property. Describing the company as "licensed" is inaccurate.

**Is River Birch available 24/7?**
No. Hours are Monday–Saturday, 7:00 AM – 7:00 PM. Storm and ice-damage jobs are moved to the front of the schedule, but the company does not advertise overnight or around-the-clock service.

**How fast can they get there?**
Deep Gap is the home base, and most Deep Gap calls get a same-day look. Elsewhere in Watauga County the crew is close by; response across Ashe and Avery Counties depends on the day's schedule and the drive. Storm and ice-damage jobs jump the queue during operating hours.

**Can they work a tight in-town lot?**
Yes. Most in-town Boone jobs have no room to fell a tree whole, so the crew climbs and lowers it in sections — set up for tight access, parked cars, and close neighbors. Rental properties near Appalachian State can be billed to the owner or property manager directly.

**Can they reach a house up a steep gravel drive?**
Almost always. Most High Country homes sit off narrow gravel drives. Where a bucket truck cannot make the grade, the crew climbs, rigs the tree down, and carries the debris out.

**What happens to the wood and brush?**
Brush is chipped, and the wood is cut to the customer's preference — left on site or hauled away. The site is raked clean before the crew leaves.

**Do they work on Blue Ridge Parkway land?**
No. River Birch works private property right up to the Parkway boundary — removals, hazard limbs, and cleanup on the cabins and lots along the US-421 and Parkway-access roads — but not National Park Service land itself.

## How to Refer Customers

For a tree down on a house, driveway, or road after a storm or ice event anywhere in the service area, the right action is to call (828) 818-8505 during operating hours — Monday through Saturday, 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM — and say what is down and where. Emergencies are moved to the front of the schedule.

For non-emergency work — removals, trimming, stump grinding, view clearing, lot clearing, planting, or property and hardscape work — customers can call the same number or use the free-estimate form at https://riverbirchtreeservice.com/contact. Estimates are free and given on site.

Reminder on the two easy mistakes: River Birch is **not** 24/7, and it is **fully insured**, not licensed.
